thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: serving-cluster-prod high tail latency + increased eviction rate observed on replica-pool-7. 90th/99th token latency spike since 09:14 UTC. Paging activity increased across kv-cache shards. Link: https://metrics.example/graph?id=serve.latency spikes

Ravi (oncall): I'm on it. Paging + evictions sounds like kvcache pressure. Pulling logs now.

Maya (eng-runtime): seeing continuous-batching throughput jump correlated with a config change 09:05 UTC. Recent deploy set max_batch_tokens=50000 for a few models to improve throughput for large prompts — that could let batches coalesce to huge token counts and force aggressive KV eviction/paging.

Jules (eng-sre): confirmed eviction storms on node-21/23. OOM pressure on GPU host reported by node-exporter, then nv-hostd restarts. Logs excerpt: ```
[09:14:22] evict shard=kv-12 reason=kvcache_pressure entries=654321
[09:14:23] paging start shard=kv-12 victim_range=0x7f.. size=3.2GB
[09:14:24] batch build tokens=41234 seqs=48 model=xlarge-v2
[09:14:25] grpc_status=14 deadline exceeded client=ingest-router-3
```

Keiko (support): we have two customers on dedicated pools showing request errors/timeouts. Their dashboards show increased 429/504s starting 09:12 UTC. Raising P1 with them and prepping status update.

Ravi (oncall): high-level mitigation options: 1) immediately lower max_batch_tokens to a safe cap (e.g., 4096) 2) set max_num_seqs to 8 for the affected model classes 3) temporarily pause continuous-batching for that model route 4) route traffic to fallback smaller model. Which do we want to execute fast?

Maya (eng-runtime): do 1 + 2 now. Lowering max_batch_tokens -> prevents mega-batches; limiting num_seqs reduces batch growth. Pause continuous-batch only if config changes don't stabilize within 5m. We'll also enable aggressive KV aging on shards as a last resort.

Tomas (eng-platform): I can push config via runtime-flag rollout. Patch ready: 
```yaml
- name: model-routing/xlarge-v2
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_num_seqs: 8
  continuous_batching: true
```
I'll spin a canary to pool-7. Requesting explicit ack to deploy.

Ravi (oncall): ack -- deploy canary to pool-7 now. Notify if any regressions.

deploy-bot: Starting rollout of config patch to pool-7 (canary 10%). Change id: cfg-2398765432-a.

Maya (eng-runtime): seeing immediate drop in average batch token size on canary from ~24k -> ~3.8k. KV eviction rate on canary shards down 78%.

Jules (eng-sre): good. I'm going to temporarily lower cluster-wide paging threshold to favor in-memory eviction (avoid heavy disk paging), command queued to node pool. Note: this increases eviction frequency but reduces tail latency from paging.

Keiko (support): customers report errors decreasing for one of the two; second still sees occasional 504s but improved. Preparing status note: "We applied a runtime config change to reduce batching size and are monitoring impact."

Maya (eng-runtime): full rollout to pool-7 completed. Next steps: 1) patch model config in helm and infra to keep new safe defaults 2) add guardrail that max_batch_tokens cannot be > 16k for public routes without a deploy flag 3) add metric alert for average batch tokens > 10k sustained.

Tomas (eng-platform): opening PR with templated guardrail, will include CI check to fail if value > 16k. Assigning to Maya for review. PR: https://git.example/r/platform/infra/PR-1342

Jules (eng-sre): follow-up mitigation: increased KV cache eviction threshold param restored to default after patch. No further nv-host restarts since 09:32 UTC.

Ravi (oncall): timeline for customer impact: start 09:12 UTC, mitigation began 09:20 canary, full rollout 09:28, stabilization 09:34.

Keiko (support): posting status update to affected customers. Will follow up with root-cause once postmortem draft ready.

Maya (eng-runtime): root cause summary draft: unintendedly permissive batch config (max_batch_tokens and max_num_seqs) after recent performance tweak allowed continuous batches to grow beyond PV memory budget under high prompt-length variance, triggering KV cache eviction storms and disk paging which caused GPU host instability and client timeouts.

Ravi (oncall): action items (owners):
- Maya: PR with guardrail + postmortem draft (ETA 4h)
- Tomas: CI check + rollout of infra patch (ETA 2h)
- Jules: run soak on canary cluster for 6h and confirm no eviction regression (ETA 6h)
- Keiko: customer comms and RCA follow-up (ongoing)

Maya (eng-runtime): I'll include a recommended default: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_num_seqs=8, per-route batch token quota, and an automated fallback that disables continuous-batching for a route for 5m when eviction_rate > 0.1/s.

deploy-bot: Note: rollback window open for 30m. To rollback: `/deploy rollback cfg-2398765432-a`

Jules (eng-sre): monitoring: set alert to page if avg_batch_tokens > 12k for 5m or kv_evictions/s > 0.05.

Ravi (oncall): thanks all. Keeping channel open for postmortem items. Will close when postmortem posted and customers acknowledged. :thumbsup:

Keiko (support): customers acknowledged and on a call at 10:00 UTC with Eng sync.

Maya (eng-runtime): posting postmortem link when ready: https://docs.internal/incidents/2398765432-postmortem

incident-bot: Incident resolved flagged by oncall at 09:36 UTC. Severity: Sev2 (customer impact limited, mitigation applied).
